campus: Civitavecchia - Polo Universitario di Civitavecchia (Department of Ecological and Biological Sciences - DEB)
academic_requirements: Open access (no numero chiuso, no TOLC), but subject to a mandatory academic-fit check ('nulla osta') via the GOMP portal plus a compulsory oral admission interview. Preferred entry: bachelor's degree in the Italian L-13 class (Biological Sciences) or a recognized equivalent foreign degree. Graduates of other bachelor's classes need at least 32 ECTS overall in: Botany (BIO/01, BIO/02, BIO/03), Zoology (BIO/05), Ecology (BIO/07), Microbiology (BIO/19), plus an adequate number of credits in other related basic disciplines (Chemistry, Mathematics, Physics). Graduates of the Italian L-32 class (Environmental Sciences) are only admitted if their L-32 degree is UNITUS's own 'Natural and Environmental Sciences' bachelor's. Applicants request the 'nulla osta' through GOMP by uploading their degree/transcript certificate (exams taken, credits, SSDs); the Study Programme Board reviews it, may require educational debts ('carenze') to be filled before enrolment, and then calls the applicant for the compulsory admission interview. Foreign qualifications require standard recognition (dichiarazione di valore / CIMEA statement) per the university-wide baseline.
language_requirements: English proficiency at a level no lower than CEFR B2 is required for enrolment (stated directly on the DEB admission-requirements page). No specific certificate list is published for this programme; the university-wide baseline applies: accepted certificates are IELTS, TOEFL, TCL, Cambridge First, PTE Academic, Oxford Test of English, Aptis ESOL General/Advanced, or documented proof (EMI certificate) that the applicant's prior university education was delivered in English. No Italian-language exam is required since the programme is taught in English.
entry_exam_or_test: No written entrance exam and no TOLC. Admission requires (1) an academic-fit ('nulla osta') review of the CV/transcript by the Study Programme Board, with any missing curricular credits to be made up before the course starts, and (2) a compulsory oral admission interview. For a.y. 2025/26 (the only published cycle at the time of this research; 2026/27 dates not yet released) interview dates were: 17 Sept 2025 (Open Day, moved up to 12 Sept 2025 10:30), 22 Sept 2025 10:00 (online), 26 Sept 2025 10:30, 20 Oct 2025 10:30, 21 Nov 2025 10:30, 19 Dec 2025 10:30, 20 Feb 2026 10:30. Interviews are held at the Civitavecchia University Campus (Piazza Verdi 1) for Italian students, and remotely for international students. International (EU and non-EU) applicants must also submit a pre-admission form (Google Form) available on the course webpage.
application_deadline_eu: No programme-specific application deadline is published (admission is rolling via nulla-osta request + interview). University-wide enrolment window for 2026/2027: 2026-08-01 to 2026-12-29 for first-year Master's students, extended to 2027-02-28 for January/February graduates. Interview dates currently published on the DEB admission page are still labelled a.y. 2025/26 (last interview 2026-02-20); 2026/27 interview dates had not yet been published on unitus.it at the time of this research.
application_deadline_non_eu: Same rolling process and same university-wide enrolment window as EU students (2026-08-01 to 2026-12-29, extension to 2027-02-28 for Jan/Feb graduates). Non-EU visa cutoff for consulate application: 2026-11-30. Non-EU students complete the same online pre-admission form and, per the DEB page, are interviewed remotely rather than in person at Civitavecchia. Universitaly pre-enrolment applies as per the university-wide baseline.
required_documents: For the 'nulla osta' curricular check: degree certificate or self-certification listing exams taken, credits (CFU) acquired and the related scientific-disciplinary sectors (SSD) for each exam (undergraduates not yet graduated may flag 'undergraduate' status and later upload the diploma)
International pre-admission Google Form (both EU and non-EU applicants)
High-school diploma (certified copy + Apostille/legalization + certified Italian translation, OR CIMEA Statement of Verification) - university-wide baseline
Bachelor's degree of at least 3 years, with same legalization options - university-wide baseline
Declaration of Value (from an Italian consulate) OR CIMEA Statement of Comparability OR ARDI Statement of Correspondence
Diploma Supplement (can replace the Declaration of Value if legalized)
Admission letter (issued after the interview and nulla osta)
Passport (for identification, per interview-booking practice at DEB)

tuition_or_fees_link.note: ISEEUP income-based tiered fees for EU/eligible students; non-EU students who do not declare ISEEUP pay a flat fee based on country-of-origin band: EUR 600 / 1,050 / 1,500 / 1,950 per year (see Annex 1 country list). Full regulation: https://www.unitus.it/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/TUITION-FEES-AND-CONTRIBUTIONS-REGULATIONS_2026-2027.pdf ; fee simulator: https://www.unitus.it/en/students/fees-and-contributions/tuition-fee-simulator/
